statement: A transaction the Host cannot read holds back the events of its own Account, and nothing else. A dispute start or finalize whose transaction the node will not give (an input or a trace that fails, null for a transaction it does not know) cannot be told to the Entity yet: the secret in its arguments, or the body of its start, is in those bytes (R-WATCH-CALLDATA). What waits is the events of that Account from the transaction's first event on, in the chain's order (a finalize's first event is the epoch advance it made, so its secrets are told before the holds that advance dissolves, R-HOLD-DISSOLVE; within an Account a later event never reaches the Entity ahead of an earlier one, R-HEIGHT-ORDER). Every other Account's events and every SecretRevealed, which is about no Account, are told at once: a stalled transaction a counterparty picked must not blind the node to the rest of the chain, the counter windows of its other Accounts among them. The held events wait in the Host's carry as the chain logged them and are read again, with the bytes, when the transaction is given or the wait ends. THE RECORD. The Entity is told `j_behind {peer, from}` when an Account begins being held (the first block held) and `j_behind_over {peer}` when it is released, the latter only once the delivery's height reaches the Entity's view; the chain facts keep the first block (`behind`). A restart begins reading at `min(view, min(behind) - 1)`, so the held events are read again; every J event is idempotent. Exposure, owed: the Entity's view moves past the held events while the Account is behind and nothing freezes the Account (the exposure of the old whole-poll stall, narrowed to one Account; backlog: freeze while behind). THE WAIT is counted in chain time. A transaction is tried at most once per head block (a tick at a head already asked reads nothing of it, so a node catching up over many polls of one head spends one try, not one per poll), and the first fault a head gives counts whatever it was: a 503, -32005 or a timeout is the same fault as any other, and none ends the wait by its own count while a forward depends on it. The wait ends, per stalled transaction, by one of two bounds. (a) The Entity has outstanding forwards to the transaction's peer: the wait lasts until the view a delivery reaches is past `lastHeard(peer)`, the least over the Entity's locked paybook entries to that peer of (the inbound hold's deadline - lag) (paybook `lastHeard`). The hub must answer upstream `lag` blocks before the inbound deadline, and the upstream's view is at most `lag` ahead of the node's (R-HTLC-CLOCK), so a secret heard at a view up to deadline - lag can still be passed up in time and a later one cannot. (b) No forward depends on it: FEW_TRIES (3) tries, one per head block, then told unread; a pruned or unknown transaction costs a few blocks, not a stall. The bound (a) is later than the onward form, onward deadline - (lag + depth + 1) = inbound deadline - hop - lag - depth - 1 with hop = reserve + lag (paybook `hopOf`), by hop + depth + 1 blocks: it never gives up while the hub could still claim, and what the extra wait costs is that one Account's later events arrive that much later; the coordinator's form (relay 10-02 23:50) gives up that much earlier, and swapping it in is a change of `last` in `lastHeard` alone, if the Account's delay is judged dearer than the claim. No `hold` bound from the hop and the deployment's slack stays: the node setting WatchConfig.slack and the refusal hold_below_zero are gone, since the wait is no longer measured from the age of the transaction but from what the Entity has outstanding.
source: coordinator relay 10-02 23:50 (171 redesign); Review A B8 on #171; builder 10-03
